\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સત્તર} (sattar)}{સત્તર (sattar)}]{\gu{સત્તર} (sattar) — seventeen}

\label{lesson:GU-C82-seventeen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for fifteen, then the Gujarati for sixteen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સત્તર}}
\textbf{\gu{સત્તર}} (\emph{sattar}) — \textquotedblleft{}seventeen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સત્તર}} (\emph{sattar}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{saptadaśa}, \textquotedblleft{}seventeen\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13146). It is \emph{sapta}, \textquotedblleft{}seven\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{daśa}, \textquotedblleft{}ten\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for seventeen to forty.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
